raw.description:
About Dastra

Dastra is a fast-growing SaaS platform dedicated to data protection, compliance and AI governance.

Our mission is simple: turn complex regulatory requirements into clear, operational and actionable processes.

We help organisations manage their data and AI-related risks while enabling them to innovate with confidence.

As we continue to grow, we are looking for a Customer Success Manager to join our Customer Success team and support our customers throughout their journey with Dastra.

Why join Dastra?

  • Join a fast-growing European SaaS LegalTech company

  • Work with Mid-Market and Enterprise organisations on complex data, AI and compliance challenges

  • Take ownership of a strategic customer portfolio

  • Become a key expert on a sophisticated SaaS platform

  • Work closely with Customer Success, Sales, Product and Tech teams

  • Join an experienced, collaborative and ambitious team

Your role

As a Customer Success Manager, you will act as the project lead for your customers’ success with Dastra.

You will manage a portfolio of Mid-Market and Enterprise customers and cover the entire customer journey, with a strong focus on onboarding, implementation, product adoption and long-term customer success.

You will become a trusted partner and expert on the Dastra platform, helping customers translate complex business, technical and regulatory challenges into concrete use cases.

Your main objectives will be to:

  • Successfully onboard and implement Dastra

  • Drive product adoption and long-term engagement

  • Support change management

  • Demonstrate the value delivered by the platform

  • Secure renewals and customer satisfaction

  • Identify growth opportunities alongside Account Managers

Your responsibilities

  • Lead onboarding and implementation projects

  • Manage a portfolio of Mid-Market and Enterprise customers as their main point of contact

  • Drive customer success through regular follow-ups and Business Reviews

  • Monitor usage, satisfaction and value

  • Anticipate risks and secure renewals

  • Identify growth opportunities alongside Account Managers

  • Build expertise in data protection, AI governance and compliance

  • Share customer insights with Product and Tech teams

Your environment

You will join our Customer Success team and report to Jérôme, our Director of Operations and co-founder.

You will work closely with our Customer Success, Account Management, Sales, Product and Tech teams.

Our customers are mainly Mid-Market and Enterprise organisations, across French and international markets.

During your first 3 to 6 months, you will progressively build your expertise on Dastra, our methodology and your customer portfolio.

Who we're looking for

  • 4+ years of experience in Customer Success, SaaS consulting, implementation, project management or a similar customer-facing role

  • Strong understanding of SaaS environments, ideally involving complex or technical products

  • Experience managing Mid-Market and/or Enterprise customers

  • Experience with onboarding, implementation, adoption and change management

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

  • Strong project management and organisational skills

  • Customer-oriented, autonomous and comfortable with complex topics

Languages

  • French: fluent, bilingual

  • English: fluent, bilingual or native level

  • German: fluent or bilingual proficiency would be a plus

You will work with both French- and English-speaking customers in an international environment.

Compensation & working conditions

  • Around €40-47k gross/year + variable compensation, depending on experience

  • Ideally based in Paris / Île-de-France

  • Hybrid working model with 2 remote days per week

  • 5 weeks of paid leave + 10 RTT days

  • Meal vouchers and company health insurance

  • Annual company seminar and regular team-building events

Recruitment process

  1. Introductory call with Julia, Talent Acquisition Specialist

  2. Interview with a member of the Customer Success team

  3. Interview with Jérôme, Director of Operations and co-founder

  4. Business case and presentation

  5. Reference check

Ready to join us?

If you enjoy working at the intersection of SaaS, technology, data, AI and regulatory challenges, and want to become a trusted partner for Mid-Market and Enterprise customers, we'd love to meet you.

About Taurus

Join the Next Global FinTech Success Story

Are you ready to be part of a bold entrepreneurial journey and help shape the future of finance? At Taurus, we're building the next-generation digital asset infrastructure, and we might just have the perfect opportunity for you.

Headquartered in Switzerland, Taurus is a leading financial technology company specializing in digital asset infrastructure. Our fully integrated, modular platform empowers financial institutions to manage the entire lifecycle of digital assets, including custody, tokenization, and trading. We are trusted by corporate & investment banks, private banks, asset managers, broker-dealers, custodians and crypto banks.

As we expand globally, we are looking for ambitious and driven individuals to join our team and help accelerate our growth. If you’re passionate about innovation, blockchain technology, and the future of finance, we want to hear from you.

Your role

Reporting to the CMO and working closely with the Head of Taurus-NETWORK Partnerships & Marketing, you will own Taurus's communication and events outside the US: PR, social media, design and collateral, and our worldwide events program. You will be the day-to-day lead for our PR and design agencies, and will work hand in hand with the marketing automation and US partnerships & events teams.

What you will do

  • PR & communication: manage our PR & communication agency day to day: press releases, announcements, media relations, interview and speaking opportunities, and the PR calendar

  • Coordinate corporate and partner announcements with internal stakeholders (product, partnerships, legal) to ensure accurate and compliant messaging

  • Social media: run Taurus's organic social media, primarily LinkedIn: editorial calendar, post production, community engagement, performance reporting and paid advertising.

  • Design & collateral: manage our design agency to deliver collateral, event materials, presentations and visual assets consistent with the Taurus brand identity

  • Brand & content: support the team on thought leadership, turning white papers, case studies, product launches and partner news into posts, articles, newsletters and event content

  • Events (worldwide, excl. US): own the events program end to end (conferences, trade shows, roundtables, client and partner events, webinars), from selection, sponsorship and budget through logistics, on-site delivery and post-event follow-up, with clear pipeline objectives for each event

  • Coordinate the global events calendar with the US events lead so that sponsorships, messaging and materials stay consistent across regions

  • Measure the impact of each event (meetings, leads, pipeline) and ensure leads are captured in the CRM and followed up, working with marketing automation and sales

  • Coherence & cadence: own a single integrated communication calendar that links content, company and partner news, client acquisition campaigns and events, so Taurus communicates regularly and with one consistent message.

Requirements

A successful candidate will have:

  • A strong background in marketing, communication and PR within a financial services and/or digital asset company

  • Expertise in Product Marketing is a plus.

  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree

  • 5+ years’ experience in communication, PR or events marketing, ideally in a high-growth B2B company

  • A proven track record of organizing international conferences and trade shows end to end, including vendor management and budget control

  • Experience managing PR and creative agencies

  • Hands-on social media experience, especially on LinkedIn; familiarity with design tools (e.g. Canva, Figma) and video tools.

  • A passion for blockchain-based software and financial technology is a strong plus

  • Obsessed with execution: driven to achieve goals

  • Enthusiastic, proactive, and a team player

  • Strong writing and communication skills

  • Attention to detail and excellent organizational skills

  • Willingness to travel regularly for events

  • Fluent in French and English

What we offer

  • An opportunity to work at the intersection of digital assets and finance

  • A skilled and experienced team, including world-renowned experts

  • A fast-paced learning environment, entrepreneurial spirit and team spirit

  • A great moment to join as the company grows and expands

  • State-of-the-art technology and IT infrastructure

  • Hybrid remote work and flexible working hours

  • Fun team events

description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Help make the world more hospitable </strong></h4> <p>The hospitality industry is uniquely human, and it deserves technology that’s just as inspiring as the people behind it. At Mews, we’re transforming the industry with a platform that helps hotels run smarter, move faster and create better guest experiences.</p> <p>You’ll work with smart, curious people who care deeply about what they do. You’ll have autonomy and the trust to make good decisions and move quickly. And you’ll enjoy a real sense of purpose as you see the impact of what we’re building.</p> <p>If you’re motivated by ownership, curiosity and meaningful impact, and are driven to deliver consistent high performance, you’ll feel at home here.</p> <h4><strong>About the role</strong></h4> <p>Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:</p></div><p>This role owns Product and Engineering for Back of House, one of the most complex, multi-service domains on the Mews platform. Back of House covers the operational core that hotel teams rely on every day, and it needs someone who can set the product direction and run the engineering behind it, together. That combined mandate, product and engineering under one person at VP level, is rare, and the scale of hospitality technology right now makes it worth doing well.</p> <p>You'll own the full domain: strategy, roadmap, and the engineering org that builds it, working closely and collaboratively with globally distributed teams across multiple time zones, and reporting into senior leadership. This isn't a narrow platform mandate. It spans product and engineering together, with the scope to make real calls on both, and the trust to run it as one connected domain.</p> <p>Back of House software has to stay reliable at all times and keep improving, without ever pausing customer delivery to get there. The next phase of this role is about applying AI directly to the systems that support hotel teams, not just internal tooling, at a scale most engineering leaders never get to work at.</p> <p><strong>What You Would Do</strong></p> <ul> <li>Own product and engineering strategy for Back of House end to end, across a genuinely multi-service architecture.</li> <li>Run globally distributed engineering teams across multiple time zones, building the structures that let them ship together.</li> <li>Build out a management team and develop senior ICs, growing a culture that holds up at scale.</li> <li>Improve reliability, performance and technical debt as ongoing disciplines, without stopping delivery to do it.</li> <li>Decide where AI genuinely belongs in the Back of House product, and ship AI-driven improvements that change how hotel teams work day to day.</li> </ul> <p><strong>AI Fluency Level 4:</strong> in this role that means going beyond using AI to move faster yourself. You'll decide where AI belongs in the Back of House product, understand the underlying models and infrastructure well enough to make real engineering calls about them, and have already shipped something where AI was a core part of the product, not a feature added on afterwards.</p> <p><em>For more information on AI fluency at Mews, please refer to <a href="https://mews.atlassian.net/wiki/x/XQOskg">AI Fluency at Mews: A Comprehensive Guide for Candidates</a> on Confluence.</em></p> <p><strong>What You Would Bring</strong></p> <ul> <li>Combined description: Qui sommes-nous ? Télécom Paris, école de l’IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) et membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris, est une grande école du top 6 des écoles d’ingénieurs généralistes françaises. La Raison d’Être de Télécom Paris est de former, imaginer et entreprendre pour concevoir des modèles, des technologies et des solutions numériques au service d’une société et d’une économie respectueuses de l’humain et de son environnement. Nous recherchons une Ingénieure ou un ingénieur de recherche et développement en IA embarquée pour rejoindre le département INFRES à Télécom Paris. Le recrutement s’inscrit dans les activités de formation et d’expérimentation en systèmes embarqués et connectés de Télécom Paris, en lien avec le financement CMA5G et les thématiques 5G, Edge AI et Internet des objets (IoT). Le poste vise à concevoir, intégrer et maintenir des plateformes matérielles et logicielles, des bancs d’essai et des démonstrateurs utilisés dans les travaux pratiques, les projets étudiants et les expérimentations menées avec les enseignants-chercheurs. Vos principales missions seront de : Développer et maintenir des plateformes expérimentales en IA embarquée et systèmes connectés. Contribuer aux prototypes, essais et démonstrateurs des activités de recherche et de formation. Participer à la préparation et à l’accompagnement des travaux pratiques et projets. Vous êtes titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac+5 minimum en informatique, électronique ou systèmes embarqués. Vous maîtrisez les langages C/C++ et Python, l’environnement Linux et les outils de gestion de versions tels que Git. Vous disposez de compétences en débogage, tests et intégration matériel-logiciel, ainsi que d’une bonne maîtrise de l’anglais technique. Des connaissances en systèmes embarqués, microcontrôleurs, firmware ou intelligence artificielle embarquée seront appréciées. Autonome, rigoureux et doté d’un bon esprit d’équipe, vous savez analyser et résoudre des problèmes. Vous possédez également de bonnes qualités relationnelles et pédagogiques, indispensables pour accompagner les apprenants, préparer des démonstrations et transmettre vos connaissances. Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? Vous travaillerez dans un environnement en plein développement, agréable, verdoyant et accessible (notamment pour les personnes en situation de handicap) à seulement 20 km de Paris (RER B et C, proximité des grands axes routiers). Vous bénéficierez de : 49 jours de congés annuels (CA + RTT) flexibilité des horaires de travail (en fonction de l'activité du service) télétravail 1 à 3 jours/semaine possible Remboursement abonnement transports en commun à 75% Proximité de nombreuses infrastructures sportives, conciergerie, parking souterrain, restauration interne... A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé Indications de rémunération : Fourchette indicative de rémunération (hors bonus annuel variable) : 33 614 - 43 000 euros bruts annuels, selon le profil et l’expérience, définie par notre cadre juridique. A savoir : nos cotisations sociales sont moins élevées que dans le secteur privé. Constitué de huit Grandes Écoles publiques : IMT Atlantique, IMT Mines Albi, IMT Mines Alès, IMT Nord Europe, Institut Mines-Télécom Business School, Mines Saint-Étienne, Télécom Paris et Télécom SudParis, et de 2 écoles filiales : EURECOM et InSIC, l’Institut Mines-Télécom anime et développe un riche écosystème d’écoles partenaires, de partenaires économiques, académiques et institutionnels, acteurs de la formation, de la recherche et du développement économique.  Pour en savoir plus : Vidéo de présentation de l’IMT : Site carrière de l’IMT : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/ Site web de l’IMT : https://www.imt.fr/ L’Institut Mines-Télécom est placé sous la tutelle du Ministère de l’Economie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique. Il emploie 3 500 personnes (fonctionnaires, contractuels en CDI et CDD) et accueille sur les différents campus 15 000 étudiants pour des formations de niveau bachelor, master et doctorat. La Direction Générale (DG) de l’Institut est chargée du pilotage de cet ensemble de 3500 agents et de la coordination des actions inter-écoles. La Direction des Ressources Humaines est chargée d’adosser la politique de gestion des ressources humaines harmonisée et cohérente avec la stratégie de développement de l’IMT et ses enjeux. Pour cela, elle anime la construction et la mise en œuvre de la doctrine collective en matière de GRH, pilote l’efficience générale et anime le partage d’expériences et l’innovation collaborative sur les sujets de GRH. Elle est composée de 14 agents. L’IMT s’est doté en 2023 d’un SIRH commun à l’ensemble de ses entités avec HR Access et 4YOU de Sopra et a mis en place une « paie sans ordonnancement préalable (PSOP) » en partenariat avec la DRFiP. Un projet a été initié en vue d’optimiser l’organisation de la fonction paie à l’IMT et les outils SIRH associés. QUELLES MISSIONS VOUS ATTENDENT AU SEIN DE L’IMT ? : Sous la responsabilité de la Directrice des ressources humaines de l’IMT, en qualité de Responsable du pôle SIRH et paie vous êtes en charge des missions suivantes : 1.Assurer l’administration fonctionnelle du SIRH : Assurer le rôle de maîtrise d’ouvrage dans la gestion des anomalies et des évolutions du SIRH (cahier des charges, recettes, préparation de la mise en production, etc.) ; Assurer la conduite du changement sur les évolutions : rédaction de modes opératoires et formation des utilisateurs ; Assurer le support aux utilisateurs ; Vérifier et analyser les comptes rendus quotidiens de travaux automatiques : calcul de paie, calcul de congés, compteurs télétravail, fabrication de fichiers pour transmission aux organismes, intégration de fichier provenant de l’extérieur, etc. ; Suivre le pilotage global du SIRH avec la DSI et SOPRA ; Gérer les référentiels : éléments de paie, mise à jour des unités organisationnelles, mise à jour des constantes, etc. 2. Coordonner la fonction paie : Animer le réseau des responsables et gestionnaires de paie des entités de l’IMT ; Déterminer le calendrier global des opérations de paie ; Assurer le lien fonctionnel avec l’agence comptable principale ; Analyser les conséquences en paie des nouvelles réglementations et diffuser les modes opératoires correspondants ; Assurer certaines opérations de paie centralisées : augmentations annuelles, bonus variables, etc. ; Gérer la relation avec le Centre des paies de l’Etat (CPE) ; Assurer le lien avec les organismes extérieurs (GMF, Alan, Ircantec, Caisse des dépôts et consignations, URSSAF, France Travail, etc.) ; Superviser et développer le dispositif de contrôle de paie a posteriori afin de garantir la qualité des opérations de paie. 3. Encadrer l’équipe du pôle : Organiser les activités du pôle ; Assurer l’encadrement fonctionnel et hiérarchique de l’équipe. 4. title: Research and Development Engineer in Artificial Intelligence - 12 months contract
description: Who we are ? Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools. The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment. Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing potential attacks, understanding the strategies available to attackers and defenders, and verifying that critical security properties are preserved. Formal verification provides rigorous methods for addressing these challenges, allowing engineers to reason about system behaviours and establish mathematical guarantees. However, applying these techniques to realistic systems remains challenging. Verification problems can involve large state spaces and complex strategic interactions, while constructing formal models and specifying security properties often requires specialised expertise. The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges by combining formal verification with artificial intelligence. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for analysing cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. The project also investigates how AI can improve the efficiency and accessibility of these verification processes. A central objective of VITAMIN-C is to integrate AI techniques into the verification workflow. On the computational side, AI models will be investigated to guide the exploration of large state spaces and prioritise promising verification strategies. By learning from previously verified models and their associated results, these components can help identify relevant search directions and reduce the computational effort required by verification algorithms. On the usability side, the project explores AI-assisted interfaces that support engineers in constructing formal models and specifying security properties. These interfaces may exploit natural-language processing and large language models to interpret engineering descriptions, suggest formal representations, and assist users throughout the verification process. In both cases, the correctness of verification results remains the responsibility of the underlying formal methods, which validate the outcomes produced or suggested by AI components. Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of AI techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on developing AI components for verification guidance, investigating natural-language and LLM-based assistance for formal modelling, and integrating these capabilities into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in the preparation of training and evaluation datasets, the development of experimental benchmarks, and the assessment of the proposed approaches in terms of effectiveness, computational efficiency, and reliability. The overall objective is to make formal verification more scalable and accessible while preserving the rigorous guarantees provided by the verification framework. Your main responsibilities will include : Carry out R&D work in artificial intelligence for formal verification Contribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom The candidate must have a solid understanding of artificial intelligence, Python programming, data processing and analysis, and software engineering. They must also be fluent in English and able to develop, train, evaluate, test and document AI components within a collaborative environment. Experience in deep learning, natural language processing (NLP/LLM), graph learning, learning-guided search or the deployment of machine learning models would be an advantage. An interest in formal verification, cybersecurity, trustworthy AI, Docker and teaching activities would also be appreciated. The role also requires strong organisational, analytical and problem-solving skills, as well as a good team spirit. The candidate must be able to communicate clearly, explain technical concepts in layman’s terms, draft documentation and contribute to teaching activities. Required qualifications and experience : the candidate must hold a five-year post-secondary qualification (Bac+5) or equivalent. Applications from candidates with a four-year post-secondary qualification (Bac+4) and at least four years’ professional experience, a three-year post-secondary qualification (Bac+3) and at least six years’ experience, or a two-year post-secondary qualification (Bac+2) and at least ten years’ experience will also be considered. Why join us? You'll be working in a fast-growing, pleasant, green and accessible environment (especially for people with disabilities) just 20 km from Paris (RER B and C suburban train lines, close to major roads). You will benefit from : 49 days annual leave (CA + RTT) flexible working hours (depending on department activity) telecommuting 1 to 3 days/week possible 75% public transport pass reimbursement Proximity to numerous sports facilities, concierge service, underground parking, in-house catering, etc. Good to know: our social security contributions are lower than in the private sector Remuneration details: Indicative remuneration range (excluding the variable annual bonus): €33,614 – €43,000 gross per annum, depending on profile and experience, as defined by our legal framework. Please note: our social security contributions are lower than in the private sector. Other information : Application deadline: 03/12/2026 Job type : 12 months contract Job description here Our recruitment is based on skills, without distinction of origin, age, gender identity, or sexual orientation, and all our positions are open to individuals with disabilities. title: Research and Development Engineer in Formal Methods - 12 months contract
description: Who we are ? Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools. The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment. Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing both potential attacks and the strategies that defenders can adopt in response. Attackers may exploit sequences of vulnerabilities to compromise a system, while defenders may react through countermeasures such as access restrictions, system reconfigurations, or Moving Target Defense mechanisms. Traditional cybersecurity analysis techniques often focus on identifying vulnerabilities and possible attack paths, with limited support for reasoning about the strategic interactions between attackers and defenders. The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges through formal verification. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for modelling and verifying cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. This approach allows the verification of security properties, such as the preservation of confidentiality and integrity, as well as the synthesis of defensive strategies against known attack scenarios. A central challenge of the project concerns the scalability of formal verification when applied to realistic cybersecurity scenarios. To address this issue, VITAMIN-C investigates symbolic and abstract model-checking techniques, together with a modular architecture supporting the integration of different verification engines. Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of formal verification techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on formal modelling of cybersecurity scenarios, strategic model checking, development and optimisation of verification algorithms, and their integration into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in experimental evaluations using cybersecurity benchmarks and industrial use cases, contributing to the development of a practical verification tool. Your main responsibilities will include : Carry out R&D work in formal methods and cybersecurity verification Contribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom The candidate must have a sound knowledge of formal methods, transition systems, verification algorithms and software development. They must be able to design, test and document research software in a collaborative environment, and have a good command of English. raw.title: Research and Development Engineer in Formal Methods - 12 months contract
raw.description:
Who we are ?

Télécom Paris, part of the IMT (Institut Mines-Télécom) and a founding member of the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, is one of France's top 6 general engineering schools.

The mainspring of Télécom Paris is to train, imagine and undertake to design digital models, technologies and solutions for a society and economy that respect people and their environment.

Modern distributed systems are increasingly complex, with multiple interconnected components, services, and autonomous agents interacting in dynamic environments. Ensuring their cybersecurity requires analysing both potential attacks and the strategies that defenders can adopt in response. Attackers may exploit sequences of vulnerabilities to compromise a system, while defenders may react through countermeasures such as access restrictions, system reconfigurations, or Moving Target Defense mechanisms. Traditional cybersecurity analysis techniques often focus on identifying vulnerabilities and possible attack paths, with limited support for reasoning about the strategic interactions between attackers and defenders.

The VITAMIN-C (VerIficaTion of A MultI-ageNt system for Cybersecurity) project aims to address these challenges through formal verification. Building on VITAMIN, an existing modular model-checking platform for multi-agent systems, the project develops methods and tools for modelling and verifying cybersecurity properties in distributed and autonomous systems. Attackers and defenders are represented as agents with specific capabilities, objectives, and available actions. Their interactions are analysed using attack graphs, temporal and strategic logics, and model-checking techniques. This approach allows the verification of security properties, such as the preservation of confidentiality and integrity, as well as the synthesis of defensive strategies against known attack scenarios.

A central challenge of the project concerns the scalability of formal verification when applied to realistic cybersecurity scenarios. To address this issue, VITAMIN-C investigates symbolic and abstract model-checking techniques, together with a modular architecture supporting the integration of different verification engines.

Within this context, the R&D engineer will contribute to the design, implementation, and evaluation of formal verification techniques for VITAMIN-C. The work will focus on formal modelling of cybersecurity scenarios, strategic model checking, development and optimisation of verification algorithms, and their integration into the existing platform. The engineer will also participate in experimental evaluations using cybersecurity benchmarks and industrial use cases, contributing to the development of a practical verification tool.

Your main responsibilities will include :

  • Carry out R&D work in formal methods and cybersecurity verification

  • Contribute to the research profile of Télécom Paris and Institut Mines-Télécom


The candidate must have a sound knowledge of formal methods, transition systems, verification algorithms and software development. They must be able to design, test and document research software in a collaborative environment, and have a good command of English.

Skills in temporal or strategic logic, model checking, symbolic methods, SAT/SMT and multi-agent systems would be an advantage. Experience in cybersecurity, attack graphs, Python/C++ programming, Docker or distributed systems would also be an asset.

The candidate must demonstrate good team spirit, rigour, organisational skills, analytical and problem-solving abilities, as well as strong communication and technical writing skills.

Education and experience : Master’s degree (Bac+5) or equivalent; or a Bachelor’s degree (Bac+4) with at least 4 years’ experience; or a Bachelor’s degree (Bac+3) with 6 years’ experience; or a two-year higher education qualification (Bac+2) with 10 years’ professional experience.

title: Senior Structural Analysis Engineer
description: About Pangea Propulsion: We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems. Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade. We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology. We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry. We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse. We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team! We are looking for a Structural Analysis Engineer in Toulouse. About the role: As a Structural Analysis Engineer, you will be a key technical contributor within Pangea Propulsion’s Structural Analysis team, operating with autonomy on thermomechanical, dynamic, and nonlinear structural problems. You will own analysis campaigns end-to-end: from problem framing, modelling, validation, to results interpretation and design recommendations - directly influencing the architecture, performance, and robustness of the next generation of propulsion systems. Within the team, you will serve as a technical reference point for advanced structural analysis methods , help shape internal best practices, and elevate the quality of analyses across projects. A core part of your role will be coaching and guiding junior and consolidated analysts, transferring knowledge, reviewing technical work, and contributing to a high-performance engineering culture. In this position, you will also take ownership of complex structural analysis problems and contribute to defining modelling strategies and analysis standards for the team. Familiarity with rocket propulsion hardware - or strong motivation to learn - will allow you to make an immediate impact. title: Senior Software Engineer - OpenCRQ
description: 🌀 The Company Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action. Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action. At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative. As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future. 🎯 The Role We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer who is curious about the modeling problem underneath cyber risk and wants to help shape a young product. You will join OpenCRQ as its fourth engineer and work across the data model, backend and product surface. Many foundations are still being defined, giving you meaningful influence beyond the features you directly own. You will shape these decisions with the squad and experienced engineering and product leaders across Filigran. We value constructive disagreement, clear reasoning and shared outcomes, and we expect everyone to ask for context, challenge assumptions and learn from one another. 🧩 The problem you would be working on Ask a CISO what a cyber risk could cost, and the answer often still begins with a color: red, amber or green, often produced by a spreadsheet disconnected from current evidence. OpenCRQ replaces that color with a financial estimate and a traceable chain of evidence: which threat actors are active, which assets they can reach, which controls have proven effective and what the remaining exposure could cost. Every step is computed from live data and must withstand a simple question from a board: “Where does that figure come from?” That is what makes this an engineering problem rather than a reporting one. OpenCRQ is Filigran’s cyber risk quantification product. It combines threat intelligence from OpenCTI, exposure and control validation from OpenAEV, and agentic workflows through XTM One. As these products become more connected, the squad will define what agents can ask of the risk model, which evidence they can use and how their answers remain safe and explainable. 🛠️ What you would work on End-to-end product ownership. Take product problems from early ideation and technical design through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. You will have the autonomy to drive the work, while using the squad to challenge assumptions and improve the outcome. The quantification engine. Turn threat frequency, control effectiveness and asset value into probabilistic loss distributions. Build general-purpose quantitative models that can evolve as assumptions and available evidence change, without losing reproducibility or explainability. The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation. Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows. The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions. 🏆 What success could look like Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have: Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users. Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it. Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible. Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle. Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them. Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on. 🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it. 👥 The squad You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation. You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows. ✨ What will help you succeed We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions. A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need. Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design. The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve. Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time. Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification. Fluent English is required. 💡 Useful, but not required Any of the following would help, but none is expected: Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification. Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks. Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP. ⚙️ The stack TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo. OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling. A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone. 🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job. We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company , and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation . You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem. ⭐ Be part of something bigger We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative. 💻 Work at the edge of what’s next We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice. 🌍 Global opportunity without borders Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us. 🧭 A culture grounded in CORE Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching. 💰 What you can expect Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen 🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture. At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status. What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify. 🚀 Ready to Join Us? Apply now and help us build the future of the cybersecurity ecosystem, together. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

  • The correlation layer. Model complex relationships across OpenCRQ, OpenCTI, OpenAEV and customer systems. Map threat intelligence, including intrusion sets, techniques, campaigns and observations, to assets, vulnerabilities, exposures and control coverage. This includes adapting OpenCRQ to open standards and schemas such as STIX and OCSF, without coupling the product to a single representation.

  • Reliable ingestion at scale. Process hundreds of thousands of findings per tenant through delta syncs, long-running backfills and feeds with imperfect timestamps. You will help design observable, recoverable pipelines while extending tenant isolation as the domain grows.

  • The agentic surface. Design the contracts used by XTM One agents and the plain-language explanations behind risk figures. Together, the squad will define what models can safely do in a product whose outputs inform board-level decisions.

🏆 What success could look like

Priorities will evolve with the product, but within your first 6 to 12 months you could have:

  • Taken a meaningful product problem from early ideation through implementation, end-to-end testing and validation with users.

  • Shaped a core part of OpenCRQ’s interconnected data model or quantification engine and documented the trade-offs behind it.

  • Made a major ingestion or calculation path more observable, recoverable and reproducible.

  • Defined or implemented a durable contract between OpenCRQ and another Filigran product or an open standard, without making the internal model brittle.

  • Helped ship risk results that users can trace back to the evidence that produced them.

  • Contributed to the open-source release and to engineering practices the growing squad can build on.

🌐 Open source, like the rest of Filigran

OpenCRQ is about to become Open source, alongside OpenCTI and OpenAEV. You will contribute visibly to a product whose risk calculations can be inspected, challenged and improved by the organizations running it.

👥 The squad

You will join two senior engineers and a staff engineer, reporting to OpenCRQ’s Engineering Manager. The squad is small enough for you to influence its direction, without working in isolation.

You will collaborate with the VP of Technology, CTO and Principal Engineers on technical standards, and with the OpenCTI, OpenAEV and XTM One teams on cross-product contracts and integrations. These relationships bring domain knowledge and broader technical context into the squad’s decisions as it grows.

✨ What will help you succeed

We do not expect you to arrive with expertise in cyber risk or every standard named below. We are looking for a strong software engineer who can learn quickly, work autonomously and use the squad to challenge and improve decisions.

  • A track record of taking complex product problems from an ambiguous idea to a validated outcome: framing the problem, making technical decisions, implementing the solution, testing it end to end and checking that it solves the user’s need.

  • Strong experience with a modern TypeScript stack and practical knowledge of PostgreSQL beyond the ORM. You treat failure modes and observability as part of the design.

  • The ability to reason about complex relationships across systems and design interconnected data models that remain coherent as concepts and integrations evolve.

  • Comfort turning quantitative concepts into maintainable software. Formal training in statistics is not required, but you should be willing to work with probability distributions, orders of magnitude and models whose assumptions evolve over time.

  • Thoughtful use of coding agents: you know where they accelerate engineering and where their output needs careful verification.

  • Fluent English is required.

💡 Useful, but not required

Any of the following would help, but none is expected:

  • Experience in cybersecurity, GRC or risk quantification.

  • Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, OCSF, MITRE ATT&CK or other open cybersecurity standards and frameworks.

  • Experience shipping features involving LLM agents, RAG or MCP.

⚙️ The stack

TypeScript end to end: React, Vite and TanStack Router on the frontend; Node.js, Fastify and tRPC on the backend; PostgreSQL with a code-first schema and Drizzle, all in one monorepo.

OpenCRQ ships as a container, both as SaaS and on customer-managed infrastructure. We use OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs, alongside Prometheus and continuous profiling.

A significant part of the design work happens at the boundaries between OpenCRQ, the rest of Filigran’s product suite and customer security tooling. You will work directly with the teams that own those systems rather than having to navigate those boundaries alone.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.

💰 What you can expect

  • Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success

  • Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate

  • 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work

  • Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you

  • Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve

  • Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen

🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify.

description: Le Groupe QUALTECH - 5 sociétés, 7 sites et 350 salariés - est un regroupement de Laboratoires spécialisés dans les analyses de laboratoire (microbiologie, biologie moléculaire, chimie, extraction d’ADN, etc), le conseil, la recherche et la formation. En rejoignant son laboratoire AGROBIO spécialisé en microbiologie, vous participez à son expertise dans le monde de la recherche et de l’analyse agro-alimentaire Vos missions Dans le cadre d'un renforcement d'équipe dans notre laboratoire AGROBIO, nous vous attendons pour prélever des échantillons (alimentaires, d’eau et de surface) et réaliser des audits dans les cuisines de nos clients situés dans la région de LYON (départements 69 42 26 01 38 42 43 et ponctuellement 73 74 71). Vous allez avoir l'opportunité de rencontrer les différents acteurs locaux et de découvrir leur activité, qu'ils soient spécialisés dans la restauration collective (crèches, lycées, maisons de retraite, restaurants d'entreprise, armé, etc.) ou plus traditionnelle. Vous êtes le 1er maillon de cette longue chaîne menant à une analyse de haute fiabilité grâce à la collaboration de chacun. description: <p>The Security Libraries team owns the customer-side integrations behind Datadog’s run-time security products — <a href="https://www.datadoghq.com/product/app-and-api-protection/">App &amp; API Protection</a>, <a href="https://www.datadoghq.com/product/workload-protection/">Workload Protection</a>, and <a href="https://www.datadoghq.com/product/code-security/">Code Security</a> — shipping and maintaining security capabilities across seven open-source language libraries (<a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-dotnet">.NET</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-java">Java</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-go">Go</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-js">Node.js</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-py">Python</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-rb">Ruby</a>, <a href="https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-php">PHP</a>) and a set of HTTP proxy integrations (Envoy, NGINX, and HAProxy), running inside thousands of production clusters worldwide.</p> <p>Recent work spans exploit prevention (RASP), WAF detections, API Security, code security (IAST and SCA), and AI-assisted onboarding. As Engineering Manager, you’ll lead part of this polyglot team, setting the technical bar and team culture while driving the pace at which new detections and AI-assisted capabilities reach customers. This is a hands-on role: you’ll balance people leadership, product and roadmap ownership, and the operational health of code that runs in production at massive scale, with room to grow into more of Datadog’s security portfolio over time.</p> <p><em>At Datadog, we place value in our office culture - the relationships and collaboration it builds and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them.</em></p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead, grow, and develop a team of roughly 4-8 library engineers — coaching, giving direct feedback, and empowering senior ICs as technical leaders</li> <li>Own team delivery and productivity: planning, milestones, reviews, and the on-call rotation</li> <li>Set product direction with Product Management and balance priorities across App &amp; API Protection, Workload Protection, and Code Security</li> <li>Stay technically close to the work — apply strong technical judgment, contribute code where it matters most, and keep quality and architecture high</li> <li>Build strong relationships and drive alignment across the language teams and product, backend, and frontend partners</li> <li>Shape team identity and culture, and own accountability when problems occur</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who You Are:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience managing a team of engineers — setting direction with Product Managers, owning a backlog, and running delivery</li> <li>A senior software-engineering background with strong technical judgment</li> <li>A track record developing people: coaching, direct feedback, and helping engineers, both senior and struggling, grow</li> <li>Strong cross-team communication, comfortable driving alignment across many stakeholders</li> <li>Experience building libraries, SDKs, developer tooling, or systems/run-time software</li> <li>Pragmatic product-engineering experience — you’ve worked with Product Managers and weighed technical trade-offs against customer impact</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to Have:</strong></p> <ul> <li>An application security background (WAF, RASP, IAST/SCA) or adjacent observability/APM experience</li> <li>Hands-on experience with one of our languages (.NET, Java, Go, Node.js, Python, Ruby, PHP) or open-source stewardship</li> <li>Experience leading distributed or multi-language teams across many stakeholders</li> </ul> <p><em>Datadog values people from all walks of life. We understand not everyone will meet all the above qualifications on day one. That’s okay. title: Distinguished Engineer
description: At Brevo, we’re not just building a CRM. With our technology, we’re helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. From emails and SMS to WhatsApp, Chat, and Marketing Automation, our tools are intuitive, powerful, and built to scale with every ambition. We give businesses a clear view of the customer journey, so they can focus on what matters: connection. As a certified B Corp , we’re proud to grow with purpose, committed to high standards of social and environmental impact, not just performance. Today, more than 500,000 businesses across 180 countries —from NGOs like Amnesty International to global brands like Carrefour, eBay, Louis Vuitton, and Michelin—trust Brevo to engage their audiences, cut through complexity, and deliver results. Our reliable technology and 75+ integrations help them create unparalleled customer experiences, without the usual tech headaches. We recently exceeded 200m ARR and reached a major milestone by becoming a Unicorn , backed by strong growth and global expansion - and we’re just getting started! The role : We are looking for a  Distinguished Engineer based in our Paris office to lead the technical transformations that are too large, too cross-cutting, or too critical to belong to a single engineering team. This is a company-wide IC role with direct report to the CTO and explicit authority to drive major technical decisions across Product Engineering, Platform, Infrastructure and Data. This isn't an advisory role, it's a mandate to change how Brevo Engineering works at a foundational level.   What you will do: You will own a small number of high-impact technical transformations end to end: architecture, implementation strategy, migration, adoption and retirement of legacy systems. Examples include: rebuilding our CI/CD and deployment architecture across hundreds of services and repositories; replacing fragmented logging and observability patterns with an OpenTelemetry-based platform backed by ClickHouse; redesigning how we use Kafka and introducing stronger platform abstractions around messaging; turning ClickHouse into a first-class internal product rather than a database consumed inconsistently across teams; defining and driving common standards around service communication, reliability, runtime architecture and developer platforms. These initiatives will cross organizational boundaries and require changes to both infrastructure and application code. Your responsibility is to own the projects end to end, driving them through every stage and resolving whatever obstacles arise until it is delivered. Who you are: You have already operated at Principal, Distinguished, Senior Principal, Fellow, or equivalent level within a significantly larger engineering organization. You have repeatedly led transformations involving hundreds of engineers or large service fleets, distributed systems and production infrastructure, complex migrations where old and new worlds had to coexist, strong technical disagreement across senior teams, and architecture decisions with broad and lasting consequences. You move fluidly between a system design discussion, a code review, a production incident, a migration plan, and an executive-level technical decision. You bring deep expertise in several of the following: Kubernetes, CI/CD, Kafka, ClickHouse, OpenTelemetry, distributed databases, service communication, developer platforms, and large-scale observability. Whoever you are, wherever you’re from, if this role speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

  • Du gestaltest unsere IT-Zukunft: Du entwickelst unsere IT-Strategie weiter und setzt passende Lösungen für unsere Unternehmensgruppe um. Du berichtest direkt an den CEO der Gruppe und trägst die Budget-, Personal- und Projektverantwortung für die IT

  • Du bringst Projekte ins Ziel: Du planst und leitest die Einführung und Verbesserung neuer Systeme – von ERP/WMS und CRM über Webshops und Produktkataloge bis zu Schnittstellen – und koordinierst interne Beteiligte und externe Partner

  • Du stärkst dein Team: Du führst und förderst zwei Mitarbeitende in Support und Applikationsverantwortung, etablierst klare Supportprozesse und Zuständigkeiten und packst im Tagesgeschäft aktiv mit an

  • Du hältst den Betrieb am Laufen: Du sorgst gemeinsam mit deinem Team und externen Dienstleistern für eine stabile und sichere IT, funktionierende Schnittstellen und eine hohe Datenqualität. Bei Störungen findest du rasch tragfähige Lösungen

  • Du modernisierst unsere Schnittstellen: Du leitest die Ablösung der bestehenden Schnittstellen mit Lobster Data und steuerst die Umsetzung mit unseren externen Partnern

  • Du machst Abläufe einfacher: Du erkennst, wo digitale Lösungen und Automatisierungen einen echten Mehrwert schaffen, und begleitest unsere Mitarbeitenden bei Veränderungen

Das bringst du mit

  • Eine abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder ein Studium in Informatik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation sowie fundiertes IT-Fachwissen und ein gutes Systemverständnis

  • Erfahrung mit anspruchsvollen IT-Projekten; die Gesamtverantwortung für die IT eines KMU ist erwünscht. Erfahrung in der Logistikbranche oder bei der IT-Integration von Unternehmensgruppen und Übernahmen ist von Vorteil

  • Nachweisbare Erfahrung in der Leitung eines ERP-Projekts ist zwingend. Du kennst die Herausforderungen von der Anforderungsaufnahme über die Datenmigration bis zur Einführung im laufenden Betrieb

  • Freude daran, ein kleines Team zu führen, Menschen zu motivieren und gemeinsam Lösungen zu entwickeln

  • Verständnis für betriebliche Prozesse und dafür, wie wichtig eine zuverlässige IT für den täglichen Logistikbetrieb ist

  • Eine klare, verständliche Kommunikation und eine ausgeprägte Kunden- und Dienstleistungsorientierung, Eigeninitiative, Verantwortungsbewusstsein und wirtschaftliches Denken. Du setzt Prioritäten, behältst die Kosten im Blick und hast Lust, im KMU-Umfeld die Ärmel hochzukrempeln und etwas zu bewegen

  • Die Bereitschaft, im Notfall auch Abend- oder Wochenendeinsätze zu übernehmen

Worauf du dich freuen kannst

  • Eine Schlüsselrolle mit direktem Draht zum CEO: Du übernimmst die IT-Verantwortung für unsere drei Unternehmen, setzt Prioritäten und treibst die Weiterentwicklung unserer IT voran

  • Echte Aufbauarbeit mit Gestaltungsspielraum: Es gibt viel aufzubauen – von zeitgemässen Systemen über klare Prozesse bis zu verlässlichen Strukturen. Dafür bietet dir die Geschäftsleitung viel Freiraum und Unterstützung

  • Die Chance, sichtbar etwas zu bewegen: Wenn dich anspruchsvolle Aufgaben anspornen und du gerne Verantwortung übernimmst, kannst du bei uns viel bewirken, zukunftsweisende IT-Lösungen umzusetzen und aktiv an der Gestaltung der digitalen Zukunft unseres Unternehmens mitzuwirken

  • Abwechslung in drei Unternehmen: Dich erwarten unterschiedliche Anforderungen, spannende Projekte und Einblicke in unsere betrieblichen Abläufe

Lust, die Verantwortung für unsere IT zu übernehmen?

Dann zeig uns, was dich antreibt und welche Erfahrungen du mitbringst – besonders aus deinem ERP-Projekt. Wir freuen uns auf dich und deine Bewerbung!

title: Product Frontend Engineer
description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. title: Account Executive
description: <h1><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>Join Proton and build a better internet where privacy is the default</strong></span></h1> <p>At Proton, we believe that privacy is a fundamental human right and the cornerstone of democracy. Since our inception in 2014, founded by a team of scientists from CERN, we have dedicated ourselves to providing free and open-source technology to millions worldwide, ensuring access to privacy, security, and freedom online.</p> <p>Our journey began with Proton Mail, the largest secure email service globally, and has since expanded to include Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive, and Proton Pass. These tools empower individuals and organizations to take control of their personal data, break away from Big Tech’s invasive practices, and defeat censorship. Our work impacts hundreds of millions of lives, from activists on the front lines defending freedom to leaders in governments protecting sensitive information. In some cases, Proton’s services have even been instrumental in saving lives by enabling secure and private communications in high-risk situations.</p> <p>Proton today supports over 100 million user accounts with a growing team of over 500 people from over 50 different countries, from the world's top companies and universities. We value intelligence, learning potential, and ambition in our hiring process. Adaptability is key as we navigate uncharted territories and redefine how business is conducted online. We believe smaller teams of exceptional talent will always prevail over larger teams with lower talent density. Proton has become profitable and reached scale without relying upon VC funding, largely due to superior talent that allows us to do things faster, more creatively, and more efficiently.</p> <p>We have a global mindset and big ambitions but remain a start-up at heart. We value empowerment and flexibility and keep our structure flat to keep moving fast and avoid unnecessary politics. Tired of blending into the crowd? title: Product Manager - Surveying & Mapping Drone
description: Join the Wingtra team and become part of this venture-backed robotics scaleup with a global and international team of 125+ dedicated Wingtranauts who want to see their actions have a positive and lasting impact on the world. Founded more than 8 years ago at ETH Zurich, Europe’s leading robotics university, our goal is to build the best aerial robots to digitize the world at the push of a button and set the basis for faster and better decisions. Wingtra provides efficient and reliable data solutions to a variety of industries ranging from mining, construction and agriculture to humanitarian organizations, environmentalists and wildlife monitoring groups. We are reaching for the stars and together we might just get there. Open communication, asking hard questions and valuing diverse viewpoints are but a few things that will help us achieve our goals. Above all we will never stop learning and striving to help each other reach our maximum potential. Now we need someone to help decide what we build next. You’ll own the priorities for our data capture platform, from the aircraft to the sensors they carry. You’ll work side by side with customers in the field, Wingtra engineers and Wingtranauts across all business functions. Your job is to find the problems that matter most to our customers and turn good ideas into products people love. Inside Wingtra you’re the voice of the user. Outside you’re the voice of the product. Responsibilities Know your customers. You spend time with survey and mapping teams in the field. You learn how they work, how they buy, what else they could use and what they still can’t do. Set the priorities. You weigh customer value, market opportunity, development effort, price and margin. Then you make a clear call on what comes next. Test ideas early. You try them with customers and engineers, learn fast and adjust. Shape the product development. You steer the capture platform: aircraft, sensors, workflows and data deliverables. You make the performance, reliability and usability trade-offs together with engineering. Take it to market. You launch with Product Marketing, Sales, Support and partners and explain why the product matters. After launch you stay close to field results and keep supporting the product through its lifecycle. Follow the outcomes. You track customer outcomes, usage and commercial results. You use what you learn to pick the next problem to solve with the team. Requirements You have a taste for great products and a relentless drive to understand what makes users love them. You make things happen. You act like an owner and hold yourself accountable to outcomes not output. You care primarily about happy customers and a successful business. You bring people with you. You listen closely, speak clearly and earn trust with customers and engineers, including when you disagree. You find a way forward. You are very comfortable with ambiguity. You work constructively with people and constraints, know when to push and when to adapt. You’ve spent 3+ years developing or deploying hardware products and their software workflows, with clear ownership of product, operational or commercial results. You have a technical background in engineering, geospatial or another technical field. You’re commercially fluent. You read a pricing model, channel margin or renewal term and see why the business cares. You’re fluent in English and happy to travel regularly to customers and partners in the US and Europe. Plus You’ve founded a relevant business of your own, led surveying or drone operations, or built products for geospatial customers. You have hands-on experience with photogrammetry, LiDAR or bringing a commercial robotics product to market. If you enjoy teamwork more than being the individual superhero, and if you thrive in a feedback-driven culture and an exciting, unconventional yet structured and progressive start-up environment, we would love to hear from you.
